content.overview: BNS s. 57 — Abetting commission of offence by public or by more than ten persons.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Abetting commission of offence by public or by more than ten persons. BNS restatement of IPC 117. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 117. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 57 is the rule on “Abetting commission of offence by public or by more than ten persons”. The section provides that whoever abets the commission of an offence by the public generally or by any number or class of persons exceeding ten, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years and with fine. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 57 exists so that “Abetting commission of offence by public or by more than ten persons” has a closed legal test in Chapter IV — Of Abetment, Criminal Conspiracy and Attempt. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: The inchoate trio. Abetment now covers extra-territorial aid; conspiracy and attempt sit next to it.

The provision in detail
57. Whoever abets the commission of an offence by the public generally or by any number or class of persons exceeding ten, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years and with fine

Essential ingredients
1. Whoever abets the commission of an offence by the public generally or by any number or class of persons exceeding ten, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years and with fine

Statutory illustrations
Illustration (a). A affixes in a public place a placard instigating a sect consisting of more than ten members to meet at a certain time and place, for the purpose of attacking the members of an adverse sect, while engaged in a procession. A has committed the offence defined in this section

Exam use: quote illustration (a), then write which ingredient of BNS s. 57 it proves. Copying the illustration without that mapping sentence does not score.

learningObjectives: Understand aggravated mass abetment under BNS s. 57.
Analyze the thresholds: 'by the public generally' or 'by more than ten persons'.
Examine the special 3-year statutory penalty for collective incitement.
enhancement.definition: BNS s. 57 provides that whoever abets the commission of an offence by the public generally or by any number or class of persons exceeding ten, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Inciting mob violence, public riots, or collective defiance of law poses grave threats to public order, justifying a distinct aggravated offence against mass instigation.
statutoryFramework: Chapter IV — Of Abetment, Criminal Conspiracy and Attempt, BNS s. 57 (corresponding to IPC s. 117).
Target group 2: 'any number or class of persons exceeding ten'.
Penalty: Imprisonment up to three years, or fine, or both.
Illustration: Affixing a public placard urging a mob of more than ten persons to attack an adversary at a specific time.
essentialIngredients: The accused abetted the commission of an offence.
The abetment was addressed to the public generally, OR to a group or class exceeding ten persons.
The abetment was committed by speech, writing, digital broadcast, placards, or assembly.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 57 addresses collective incitement. While ordinary abetment is usually targeted at specific individuals, modern rabble-rousing, hate speech, inflammatory posters, and viral social media broadcasts target anonymous masses. If a person affixes posters in a market or circulates digital messages urging an entire community or a crowd of fifty people to burn down a commercial building, s. 57 applies directly. The crime is complete upon publishing or uttering the mass incitement, regardless of whether anyone obeys.
examples: Teaching example (Inflammatory placard): A affixes in a public square a placard inciting the public to gather in a mob exceeding ten persons and attack a government depot. A is guilty under s. 57.

Teaching example (Social media incitement): An influencer posts a video calling upon a crowd of hundreds of followers to vandalize toll booths on a national highway. Section 57 directly penalizes the influencer.
distinctions: Mass abetment (s. 57) vs Individual abetment (s. 45/49): Section 57 specifically addresses diffused incitement to the public or groups exceeding 10 persons.
Abetment of mob offence vs Unlawful Assembly (s. 189): Section 57 punishes the instigator; unlawful assembly punishes active membership in the mob.
problemApplication: Issue: Whether an agitator who delivered a public speech urging an assembly of thirty union workers to assault factory management can be prosecuted under BNS s. 57.
Rule: Section 57 penalizes whoever abets the commission of an offence by any number of persons exceeding ten.
Application: The audience exceeded ten persons (thirty workers), and the speech directly urged physical assault.
Conclusion: The agitator is guilty of mass abetment under s. 57.

Punishable with up to 3 years imprisonment, or fine, or both.
Applies to posters, speeches, and viral digital broadcasts.
